title: Decision-context snapshots + per-hop micro-metrics for routing observability
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Current routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) are opaque in production. When an application sees a sudden latency spike or quality regression, engineers must stitch together traces, logs, and model metrics manually across services. This increases MTTI and makes causal attribution of bad outputs or increased cost difficult.

Goal: Provide lightweight, privacy-conscious decision-context snapshots and per-hop micro-metrics for every routed request (sampled). Snapshots should capture the routing inputs, chosen route (region, tier, model variant), routing score vector, fallback reason (if any), and compact per-hop timings and token counts. These will power: fast RCA, SLO alerts with decision-attribution, and model variant regression detection.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end latency from request to routing-decision log emission < 3ms added p99 on critical path when sampling is off.
- Collected snapshots at 5% uniform sampling with adaptive burst control.
- Dashboard that shows route-level error/latency attribution and top fallback causes within 1 iteration of a deploy.
- No PII or request content stored in decision snapshots; all request payloads are referenced by hashed IDs with KMS-wrapped pointers for accounts that opt-in.

Design approach summary:
1) Decision Context Snapshot: a compact protobuf-like JSON string (but stored as opaque blob) containing: request_hash, route_id, route_attributes (region,tier,model_variant), routing_scores (list of name:score pairs), timestamp, fallback_reason (nullable), policy_version, and a short provenance trace_id that links to the platform trace. Intentionally minimal to avoid token leakage.

2) Per-hop micro-metrics: for each hop in the routing pipeline (policy-evaluator, region-router, capacity-check, model-resolver, fallback-resolver), emit micro-latency (ms), queue_time (ms), token_estimate, and decision_flags. These are emitted as metrics tagged with route_id and policy_version, and as a compressed per-request event when sampled.

3) Adaptive sampling: baseline sample rate 5% with a token-bucket burst allowance and anomaly-triggered upsampling (e.g., when p99 latency or error rate exceeds thresholds, temporarily sample 100% for 60s). Sampling decisions are deterministic per-request using a trace-derived hash to help playback.

4) Storage and retention: sampled decision snapshots go to a hot Kafka topic for 48h then roll up into aggregated daily stores (ClickHouse) for 90d retention. Raw blobs are TTL'd and optionally archived for enterprise customers. Access controls enforced via existing RBAC and audit logging.

5) Instrumentation & schema evolution: schema version in each snapshot; the console will show human-readable interpretations for known policy versions. We will add a compatibility layer for older snapshots during rollouts.

Privacy & security: No request text, user IDs, or embeddings are stored in snapshots. For customers who opt-in to full traceability, we will store encrypted pointers that reference customer-managed storage (KMS/HSM). Security review required before merging.

Observability UX: Add a new console view "Routing Insights" with per-route waterfall visualization, most-common fallback reasons, and an interactive trace sampler that can open the full trace when available.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Internal-only sampling for 5% traffic in prod, basic dashboard, no customer opt-in hooks (2 sprints).
- Phase 2: Tenant-aware storage and opt-in archive for enterprise (1 sprint).
- Phase 3: Anomaly-triggered upsampling and automated RCA stories that create tickets when regressions detected (2 sprints).
comments: 2025-02-11: Initial design review with runtime team. Agreed to keep snapshot schema minimal; avoid storing request payloads. Action: Maya to draft snapshot schema and sampling policy.
2025-02-18: Security sync – legal requested explicit gating for PII and opt-in mechanics. Added security_review_required flag. Action: schedule threat model review.

2025-02-24: Implementation spike complete. Prototype writes opaque decision blobs to kafka topic 'routing.snapshots.v1'. Observed 0.6ms median overhead when sampling disabled, 2.4ms added at 5% sampling in canary cluster.
2025-02-28: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342 - adds snapshot emitter and per-hop micro-metrics instrumentation. Need review from infra and observability teams.
2025-03-03: UX stub for console view added. Liam O'Connor prototyped waterfall visualization. Next: link sample blobs to console and implement deterministic sampling using trace-hash.
2025-03-03: Blocker identified: ClickHouse schema needs additional columns for route_id and policy_version to support aggregations. Filing ENG-51801 to extend schema.
2025-03-03: Next steps: finish threat model, add automated test for sampling determinism, land PR, and enable 5% sampling in prod canary next week.
